feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 4 (mass 0.6 kg, +/-0.05 m, 16 mm, base_speed 1.3) had oval line loss at 0, but S-bend at 0.95 events and slalom at 1.0 event, with max_error about 0.063 m and progress 0.16 and 0.11. Iteration 3 at 0.7 kg gave nearly the same result, so mass has little effect on overshoot. Iteration 0 at base_speed 1.8 gave the worst S-bend progress (0.04) and iteration 1 at 1.4 gave 0.165, so bend entry speed looks like a controller lever, not a geometric one. Decide the next geometry from the next race as follows. If S-bend and slalom line_loss_events are still 1 with geometry unchanged, the loss is not geometric, so do not edit geometry; the Integrator will check line_loss handling and the start pose. If line_loss_events is 0 on all three tracks but max_error still approaches 0.06 m, the bends need more turn authority, so test wheel_track 0.12 m. If max_error stays near 0.06 m with no line loss after that, test mass 0.5 kg. If runs complete but completion_time exceeds 2.5 s, test wheel_radius 0.035 m for more top speed.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events is 0 on all three tracks but max_error still approaches 0.06 m, set wheel_track to 0.12 m. Iterations 3 and 4 showed the 0.06 m off-track limit cannot move with body_width, and this gives more differential turn authority for the bends.

If max_error stays near 0.06 m with no line loss after the wheel_track change, set mass to 0.5 kg. Iteration 4 showed 0.7 to 0.6 kg moved max_error only from 0.064 to 0.063 m, so test a larger step before concluding mass is irrelevant.
If runs complete but completion_time exceeds 2.5 s, set wheel_radius to 0.035 m for more top speed. Progress is the current limit (0.11 to 0.17), so do not change wheel_radius before runs finish.
